payload.title: harness._corpus_git is a private git runner that omits the safe.directory rule of main_anchor._git and treats every nonzero return as 'not a commit' or 'not an ancestor', so a corpus repository owned by another uid read as root (git exit 128, dubious ownership) is refused as a missing corpus commit
evidence: tools/aria-acceptance/harness.py:679-687 (_corpus_git: scrubbed env, no safe.directory, subprocess.run with a timeout that is not caught)
tools/aria-acceptance/harness.py:695-701 (any returncode other than 0 from rev-parse --verify or merge-base --is-ancestor becomes baseline_exam_corpus_commit_missing)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/main_anchor.py:243-267 (the kernel's scrubbed runner names the checkout in a command-line safe.directory when root reads a root-owned repo)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/main_anchor.py:97-104 (scrubbed_git_env, the part the harness does share)
payload.rule_violated: Single center for hermetic git: a second scrubbed-env runner without the owner's trust rule or exit-code discipline (rev-parse --verify --quiet and merge-base --is-ancestor return 1 for 'no', 128 for a fault).
payload.notes: Sessions here run as root while the CI runner's checkouts belong to uid 1001 (root's global git config carries safe.directory entries for the runner's paths). git refuses such a repo with 'fatal: detected dubious ownership' and exit 128 (reproduced here on a repo owned by uid 1001: rev-parse --verify --quiet HEAD^{commit} returns 128 under root's home config and 0 only with -c safe.directory). _corpus_git has no such scope and the harness reads 128 as 'not a commit of <repo>', so a valid corpus is reported missing with a misleading name and the real cause is dropped; the same conflation applies to --is-ancestor. The refusal direction is safe; the diagnosis is wrong, and a timeout raises an unnamed TimeoutExpired. Close condition: Run the corpus checks through one shared hermetic git runner that carries the safe.directory rule, and map only exit 1 to the 'missing' and 'not an ancestor' refusals, naming any other exit (128, timeout) as its own refusal. Add a test with a repo owned by another uid that expects the named fault, not corpus_commit_missing. Verified at origin/main ae2958653d.
